newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - FRANCE - LE MONDE MAY 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FRANCE - LE MONDE MAY 28.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.

-- Centre-right coalition remains puzzled after a televised address by President Jacques Chirac Tuesday, while socialist party leader Lionel Jospin prepares for a possible win in Sunday's parliamentary election runoff.

-- Former CCF and Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean-Maxime Leveque remanded in custody as part of an investigation by judge Eva Joly into alleged misuse of funds at bank IBSA. The bank became a subsidiary of Credit Lyonnais in 1990 and came close to bankruptcy and is now held by the CDR company in charge of selling off dubious Credit Lyonnais assets.
-- State considering buying Credit Lyonnais's stake in Pinault Printemps Redoute.
-- PSA chairman Jacques Calvet forecasts a 13.3 percent fall in new car registrations in France in 1997 over 1996.

-- LVMH said it would buy all Guinness'interests in their joint ventures, gaining the right to continue marketing and distributing Guinness brands in key markets such as China, the U.S., France, Hong Kong and Japan for at least 10 years. LVMH has a 14.2 percent holding in Guinness.
